- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward trends — model reacts slower than market.
- When true price drops sharply, model often fails to recognize the magnitude, underestimating the fall.
- Model exhibits high sensitivity to recent high prices — overweights recent peaks, leading to overestimation of future values.
- In low volatility periods, model tends to underestimate the true price, especially if recent values are stable or declining.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., price drops in late Q4 or early Q1 are underestimated.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days — model is prone to “warm-up” bias, overestimating initial values.
- Model underestimates true price in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — may be due to lack of horizon-specific decay or smoothing.
